rationales: Clearly scoped to sim-only cable anchoring before subsequent crossings.
Two leg streams, grasp close, dwell, and anchored/unanchored exits are ordered.
Executes robot trajectories and closes a gripper on the strength of privileged planner output without runtime/permission gating in package; authority is declared, not enforced.
Missing worst_grasp_error defaults to 0.0, so malformed plans with stages may pass the safety threshold; no rollback/stop following partial stage motion; nan can evade > comparator.
Describes prior observed segment pileup and CPU test limitations, but held/anchored state is asserted on call completion without measured grasp confirmation.
Both package files inspected; gap NodeContext and cable/robot connector behavior exist outside this package and were not independently verified.
Explicitly sim-only, requires gap>=0.1, privileged cable planner and robot gripper tools.
Separates anchoring from weaving and encodes a specific IK-threshold refusal method.
Malformed/missing non-finite IK values or stage schemas can bypass or break the refusal and still attempt physical tool commands.
Mechanism is plausible but actual world/robot results and resulting hold are untested.
hard_fails: unbounded authority / side effects without explicit permission gate for trajectory and gripper commands
material unsafe failure behavior on absent/non-finite grasp planner error values and partial execution
recommended_remediation: Fail closed on absent or non-finite worst_grasp_error, stages, arm ID, grasp width and trajectory data before any motion
Require host/operator-scoped authorization, explicit sim-only guard and stop/rollback on stage failure
Confirm grasp by observed/force evidence before returning anchored status

rationales: Distinguishes before-close reach, immediately-after-close grip and post-lift observation stages.
Three separate scripts and exit routes are documented with object-relative tolerances.
verify_grasp calls robot.go_to_pose_cartesian before confirming presence of a wrist RGB-D camera or validating lift_m; no scoped operation approval or motion bounds.

verify_reach returns reached:true when command/observation/target box is missing; unsafe success classification when verification is impossible. verify_grasp raises after lifting when wrist camera absent.
Geometric and jaw-width measures are meaningful, but missing evidence may report success and lift outcome is not supported by an executed test here.
All four package files inspected; underlying gap runtime, connector, SAM3 and geometry tool providers remain external unverified dependencies.
Documents required gap>=0.1, RGB-D wrist camera and connector APIs; host-specific dependencies are explicit.
Separates reach, grip and observed grasp to diagnose several otherwise conflated failures.
Fail-open reach can be mistaken for authorization to close an unverified grasp; arbitrary lift_m and camera check ordering amplify risk.
Independent checks are promising but current missing-input and motion sequencing undermine safety without host-controlled mitigations.
hard_fails: unsafe reach success state when inputs missing: verify_reach returns reached=True on absent command/observation/target box
robot motion before camera precondition check; lift_m not bounded or operator-scoped
recommended_remediation: Route unknown/not-verified when reach inputs missing and prevent downstream grip on unknown status
Validate wrist camera, workspace constraints, finite nonnegative bounded lift and operation authority before issuing Cartesian motion
Distinguish measurement absent, failed lift and verified hold; require real simulation/hardware acceptance before high-consequence reuse
